To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Li Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation in the TP53 gene.

TP53 has a role in the immune response to cancer, the TP53 gene product p53 is a key regulator of the pre-cancer niche in LFS, and the pre-carcinogenic niche in LFS can be targeted with pharmacologic interventions.
the TP53 pathway is involved in a number of processes that are relevant for the development of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the TP53 gene in the development of cancer, with a focus on the role of TP 53 in cancer initiation, and the role of the micro-environment in cancer initiation.
the role of the microenvironment in cancer development, and how this may be altered to reduce the risk of cancer.
the relationship between the host microenvironment and cancer initiation and progression, with the ultimate aim of identifying new therapeutic approaches to reduce the cancer risk in LFS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pre-cancer niche is primed for cancer, and that it is the role of the clinician to ensure that the pre-canceric environment does not become a cancer environment.
the host environment, and in particular the host microenvironment, is an important determinant of cancer initiation in LFS.
LFS is not just a TP53 disease but rather a TP53 disease that is also a disease of the host environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LFS is a disease that can be managed by targeting the pre-cancer niche.
TP53 is not only the guardian of the genome, but also the guardian of the host.
the TP53 mutation in LFS is a marker for a pre-cancerous environment that can be targeted by existing therapies to reduce the risk of cancer initiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TP53 protein has a much broader range of functions than previously appreciated.
LFS is more than a p53 story and that the host microenvironment is a critical part of the LFS story.
there is much more to LFS than the p53 gene alone and that the host environment is an important component of this.
